reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Frogs That Rode Snakeback (Book III) and its ending on the Butter-blinded Brahman page; the frame (the crow minister Live-Strong telling King Cloudy) is stated correctly.
The snake's curse story is kept with the boy's death in one calm sentence, needed for the plot; caste is dropped with disclosure and the narrator never says the curse is real.
The inner tale (adultery, a killing, a mutilation) is omitted and disclosed; Water-Foot's unease and the snake's 'nothing at all' are kept.
Age band 12+: all the frogs, the king included, are eaten on the king's own order; this is said plainly, never drawn, and the content note says so. Animals in the neuter; no em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured at x=512 and y=512/1024; painted to every edge with no text. One gpt-5.6-sol generation, no edits.
The old grey-black cobra, the frog king with his yellow flower crown and the small green frogs are consistent; the frogs on the snake grow fewer from panel 3 to 5 and panel 6 shows an empty pond.
No eating, fangs, bones or death is drawn; the snake's mouth is closed in every panel. The second snake in panel 5 is jet-black and clearly distinct.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
